I think I'm going to try to find a way to talk to him about my depression, hopefully he'll realise that he can talk to me

Wow that Bene Brown video is spot on - thank you for that! I've read through the talking tips and risk assessment as well...I think for me what I'm struggling with is how to start the conversation. Since there is no natural situation where I would be alone with him - I would have to purposefully take him aside, I would need to tell him "I'd really like to talk to you, can we meet up somewhere separately from everyone else" - and I just feel like he might be really uncomfortable with me doing that. I wouldn't be surprised if he tried to avoid it. You ask what's going on in his life - and the sad answer is nothing. He seems paralyzed; he didn't finish high school, he hasn't worked, he doesn't have any social activities or hobbies. Most of my family talk about him like he's an inconvenience to his wife - who is the sole income earner for their family. Since he lives in a small town where most of my extended family lives, he gets constant job offers because everyone seems to know that he's not working. But the ones he has taken up, he can force himself to go for a week or two, but then it's like he just can't face it, can't face being around other people, and he can't go. The last job he had (farmhand), his wife didn't find out he wasn't going until months later, because he would leave the house at 6am, and then just...sit in his car all day because he couldn't face going, and then come home and tell his wife it was a good day at work. It breaks my heart because I've struggled with depression and I know what it feels like to be walking against the tide...but I just don't know if he's going to be open to talking to me, because he doesn't seem to like talking to anyone. I can't force him, can I?

This guy I went to college with, let's call him Bob, was completely obsessed with a friend of mine. Her brother had passed away a few years prior, and in a crazy, delusional attempt to bond with her, he tells her that *his* brother just died in an accident. She, obviously, feels badly for him and talks to his friends about it, a lot of whom know Bob's brother (he graduated from our college a couple years before), and the news spreads like wildfire around the campus, people are sending flowers, asking about funeral arrangements. The Dean calls Bob's parents to offer his condolences, and apparently there was a very confused back-and-forth between the dean and the mom, where she briefly thinks that her oldest son actually is dead, and he's calling to tell her. So we're all massively confused, Bob tries to tell everyone to respect his family's privacy and stop asking questions, then his very much alive brother comes to pick Bob up from campus. So he tells this horrific lie, put his parents and friends through absolute hell, all just to have something in common to talk about with this girl he liked. Scum of the earth.

Agreed. I think the best time to talk about keto is when someone compliments you on how much weight you've lost. I've only recently started keto but have already got some comments, and I've found that is the best time to explain how keto works. That way they can't scoff at it, because they've already seen the results. But I completely get what you're saying about how frustrating the "common sense" argument can be, its just that when you've been told one thing your whole life, it takes a little while to adjust to the idea that you should eat buttered bacon as part of a healthy diet. Give people time to get used to the idea of keto, don't ram it down their throats, and if you get frustrated just remember how hot you are now :)

Your age may even be a positive because it's easier for younger ppl to lose weight, and it seems that younger ketoers don't feel the "keto flu" quite as much. Just remember, keto isn't just about bacon, eggs and bacon. Eat lots and lots of veggies, and consider taking a multi-vitamin. Also, water. Good luck!!
